title: Team A's win rate beats Team B — is B underperforming?

scenario.role: You're the RevOps analyst at Vantage
scenario.situation: The VP of Sales is reviewing the two account-executive pods. Team A closed 37% of its opportunities last year; Team B closed just 30%. She's ready to reshuffle Team B — maybe move its pipeline to A, maybe put B on a performance plan. Before she does, she wants you to confirm the read from the opportunity-level data.
scenario.stakeholderBelief: "Team A wins 37% of deals, Team B only 30%. Team B is clearly the weaker pod — let's move their pipeline to A."
scenario.question: Is Team B actually worse at closing? Compare the teams fairly and tell the VP whether B is underperforming.

columns.name: team
columns.description: Which pod owned the opportunity: A or B

columns.name: deal_size_band
columns.description: Deal size tier: smb, mid, or enterprise

columns.name: deal_value_k
columns.description: Opportunity value in thousands of dollars

columns.name: won
columns.description: 1 if the opportunity was won (closed-won), else 0

guidingQuestions: Confirm the headline: what are the overall win rates for Team A and Team B? (37% vs 30%.)
What kinds of deals does each team work? Compare the deal_size_band mix for A vs B.
Win rates fall as deals get bigger. Within each band (smb, mid, enterprise), which team wins more?
Why does Team B win within every band but lose overall? Which variable creates the reversal?
What do you tell the VP — is B underperforming, and would moving B's pipeline to A actually help?
suggestedApproach: Reproduce the overall win rates for A and B so you're testing the exact claim.
Before ranking the teams, check what each is actually working. Compare their deal_size_band mix — are they even playing the same game?
Win probability depends heavily on deal size. Compare the teams within each band so you're holding difficulty constant.
If one team wins every band but loses overall, the deal mix is doing the work — standardize both teams to a common band mix.
Recommend based on the like-for-like comparison, and flag what moving pipeline between differently-loaded teams would really do.

notebook.intro: Five steps: reproduce the win rates, check what each team is actually working, then compare them at equal difficulty.

cells.title: Reproduce the win rates
cells.explain: Start with the exact claim — Team A's win rate against Team B's.
cells.code:
rates = df.groupby("team")["won"].mean() * 100
headline_gap = rates["A"] - rates["B"]
print(f"headline gap (A - B): {headline_gap:+.2f} pts")
rates.round(2)
cells.reads: The gap is real in the data. Whether it says anything about the teams is the open question.

cells.title: Check they are playing the same game
cells.explain: Before ranking anyone, look at what each team is working. Compare the deal_size_band mix side by side.
cells.code:
mix = pd.crosstab(df["team"], df["deal_size_band"], normalize="index") * 100
print("pipeline by deal size, per team (%)")
mix.round(1)
cells.reads: The two teams are not working the same pipeline. One is carrying far more of the hardest band.

cells.title: Compare within each band
cells.explain: Win probability depends heavily on deal size, so compare the teams inside each band and hold difficulty constant.
cells.code:
by_band = df.groupby(["deal_size_band", "team"])["won"].mean().unstack() * 100
by_band["gap"] = by_band["A"] - by_band["B"]
by_band.round(2)
cells.reads: Read the gap column band by band, then compare it with the headline gap from cell 1.

cells.title: Standardise both teams to one mix
cells.explain: Give both teams the same pipeline composition and re-compute, so neither is helped or hurt by what it was handed.
cells.code:
within = df.groupby(["deal_size_band", "team"])["won"].mean().unstack()
weights = df["deal_size_band"].value_counts(normalize=True)
adjusted = within.mul(weights, axis=0).sum() * 100
adj_gap = adjusted["A"] - adjusted["B"]
print(f"mix-adjusted gap (A - B): {adj_gap:+.2f} pts")
adjusted.round(2)
cells.reads: On a like-for-like pipeline the ranking reads differently from the headline.

cells.title: Put the two numbers side by side
cells.explain: The comparison a decision should rest on, against the one that prompted the question.
cells.code:
pd.DataFrame(
    {"A - B (pts)": [headline_gap, adj_gap]},
    index=["headline", "same pipeline mix"],
).round(2)
cells.reads: Moving pipeline between the teams on the strength of the headline would reward the easier book, not the better team.

teachingNote.naiveRead: Team A closed 37% of its opportunities; Team B closed 30%. A 7-point gap looks decisive — Team B is the weaker pod, and shifting its pipeline to A should lift overall win rate.
teachingNote.theTrap: The two teams aren't working the same deals. Team A's book is mostly SMB (small, easy-to-close) deals; Team B's is mostly enterprise (large, hard-to-close) deals. Win rates fall steeply with deal size, so A's easy mix inflates its overall rate and B's hard mix deflates its. Compare within each band and the picture flips: Team B wins MORE than A among SMB deals (+4.6 pts), mid deals (+6.9 pts), AND enterprise deals (+5.8 pts). B is the stronger closer at every level; the raw rate just reflects who was handed the easy pipeline.
teachingNote.honestAnswer: Standardize both teams to a common deal-size mix and Team B is about +5.7 points BETTER than Team A, not 7 points worse. B is the more effective pod; it only trails on the headline because it carries the hard, enterprise-heavy book. Moving B's pipeline to A would hand harder deals to the weaker closer and likely LOWER total wins — the exact opposite of the intended fix.
howToGetThere: Confirm the overall win rates: A ≈ 37%, B ≈ 30% (the VP's 7-point gap).
Profile the mix: A is SMB-heavy, B is enterprise-heavy — and win rate drops sharply from SMB to enterprise.
Compare within band: B beats A among smb (+4.6), mid (+6.9), and enterprise (+5.8) deals.
Reconcile: B wins every band yet loses overall because it's overweight on hard enterprise deals — Simpson's paradox.
Standardize: weight each band's B-minus-A gap by the overall band mix → B is ~+5.7 pts better.

numbers.label: Overall win rate — A vs B

teachingNote.lesson: Comparing raw rates between groups that face different difficulty is comparing apples to oranges. A headline win rate blends skill with the deal mix a team happens to carry — so a stronger closer working harder deals can post a lower number. Before ranking people or teams, hold the difficulty constant: compare within like-for-like segments and standardize to a common mix. Here Team B is better at every level; rewarding the raw rate would punish the stronger team and hand hard deals to the weaker one.
